text: To evaluate the integral over the whole real line of cos(x)/(1 + x^2) by residues, one typically:
choices: closes the contour in the lower half-plane and uses a residue at x = 1
writes cos(x) = Re(e^{ix}), closes in the upper half-plane, and uses Jordan's lemma to kill the arc
expands cos(x) as a Taylor series and integrates term by term
uses only the residue at infinity
explanation: One replaces cos(x) by the real part of e^{iz}, so the integrand decays in the upper half-plane; Jordan's lemma sends the semicircular arc's contribution to zero, leaving 2*pi*i times the residue at z = i. Closing in the lower half-plane fails because e^{iz} blows up there.
